title: A Kitchen for the Postcard Anew
premise: Coral Joubert, a ghostwriter who has built her career on erasing herself, is hired through an anonymous literary agency to co-write a memoir via letters with an unnamed partner. She slowly realizes her pen-pal is Theo Marchand, the rival chef whose bestselling cookbook she secretly wrote and whose family she believes destroyed her mother's island restaurant. As their letters turn from hostile to intimate, Coral must choose between exposing the Marchands' land-grab of the harbor district and trusting that Theo, who has discovered her identity, is genuinely trying to make restitution. At the last ferry of the season, she chooses him and the truth together, testifying against his uncle's corrupt development deal while claiming authorship of both their books.
about_author: Lena Nakamura spent a decade as an uncredited ghostwriter for celebrity memoirs before turning to fiction under her own name. She writes about people who lend their voices to others and must finally learn to speak.

chapters.title: The Anonymous Address
chapters.summary: Coral accepts a lucrative ghostwriting assignment brokered by a discreet agency: exchange letters with an unnamed partner and shape their shared story. Her POV establishes her invisibility as armor. Beat: cautious hope masked as professionalism.

chapters.title: First Ink
chapters.summary: The first letter arrives sharp, condescending, clearly from someone famous protecting his legend. Coral answers with deliberate provocation, refusing to flatter. His POV shows irritation curdling into curiosity. Beat: sparks struck in anger.

chapters.title: Salt on Every Page
chapters.summary: Through alternating letters, they argue about food, memory, and who owns a recipe. Coral recognizes details of the Marchand kitchen she once ghost-described. Rising dread: her partner may be Theo Marchand himself. Beat: recognition and denial.

chapters.title: The Rival's Handwriting
chapters.summary: A postmark confirms it: Theo. Coral considers quitting but needs the fee to save her rented cottage on Belle-Île. She stays, telling herself she'll stay anonymous. Beat: complicity chosen for survival.

chapters.title: What My Mother Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Coral watching officials shutter her mother's harborside restaurant after a Marchand-linked developer's complaint. Present-day Coral channels grief into coldly brilliant letters. Beat: wound reopened.

chapters.title: Confessions Without Names
chapters.summary: Theo writes, unprompted, about his uncle Victor's corruption and the guilt he carries over the family's rise. He doesn't know he's writing to the Joubert daughter. Coral's hands shake reading it. Beat: sympathy invading hatred.

chapters.title: Deadline at the Harbor
chapters.summary: Victor's development company moves to demolish the old market quarter before the season ends. Coral attends the protest anonymously and spots Theo defending the demolition on camera. Beat: betrayal reconfirmed, fury sharpened.

chapters.title: The Letter That Wasn't Sent
chapters.summary: Coral drafts a furious exposure letter, then burns it. Instead she asks Theo, in-character, what he would do if he met someone he'd wronged without knowing. His answer undoes her. Beat: mercy considered.

chapters.title: Off the Page
chapters.summary: The agency forces a mid-project video call. Voices replace ink; attraction becomes undeniable. They agree to meet 'as strangers' at the island book fair, each hiding their real identity. Beat: desire outrunning caution.

chapters.title: Two Strangers, One Table
chapters.summary: They meet at the fair and connect instantly, each pretending not to know who the other is. A shared plate of her mother's signature dish nearly breaks Coral's composure. Beat: intimacy achieved on false ground.

chapters.title: The Unmasking
chapters.summary: Over dinner, names are exchanged. Theo realizes Coral is the ghostwriter behind his rival's memoir; Coral realizes he already suspected. The evening detonates into mutual accusation. Beat: the lie collapses.

chapters.title: Silence Between Postmarks
chapters.summary: Both withdraw. Theo discovers Victor forged the original complaint against the Joubert restaurant. Coral finds Theo's private ledger documenting the land scheme. Each holds a weapon aimed at the other's heart. Beat: stalemate of hurt.

chapters.title: Uncle Victor's Offer
chapters.summary: Victor, learning Coral's identity, offers her money and credit on a Marchand imprint if she buries the ledger. Power's corruption made personal. She refuses, and he threatens to expose her ghostwriting contracts. Beat: coercion tightening.

chapters.title: The Rival's Memoir, Finished
chapters.summary: Coral completes the rival memoir she's been secretly writing all along, embedding evidence of Victor's methods in its final chapters. Writing as weapon. Beat: agency reclaimed through craft.

chapters.title: Theo Breaks Rank
chapters.summary: Theo publicly resigns from the family company at a press event, naming Victor's fraud, knowing it will cost him everything including the restaurants bearing his name. Beat: duty sacrificed for justice.

chapters.title: The Burned Bridge
chapters.summary: Victor retaliates: Coral's authorship leaks, clients abandon her, and Theo's testimony is smeared as a lover's favor. Both hit professional bottom, apart. Beat: despair at full depth.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Proves
chapters.summary: Coral and Theo reunite to build the case together, matching her mother's old documents with his ledger. Working side by side, old anger transmutes into something steadier. Beat: partnership rebuilt on truth.

chapters.title: Hearing at the Prefecture
chapters.summary: The corruption hearing. Coral testifies about her mother; Theo testifies against his own blood. Victor's empire cracks under documentary weight. Beat: justice outside and inside the law at once.

chapters.title: Bylines
chapters.summary: In the fallout, Coral claims public authorship of every book she ghosted, including Theo's first cookbook. The industry reels; she stands unbowed. Theo asks her to write something new, with her name alone on the cover. Beat: visibility embraced.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Winter closes the island crossing. On the final departure, Coral almost boards alone, old habits whispering retreat. Theo runs the pier with a letter he never mailed. She steps off the gangway into his arms. Beat: the whole heart risked.

chapters.title: A Kitchen for the Postcard Anew
chapters.summary: Spring: they reopen Coral's mother's restaurant, its walls papered with postcards from readers of their published joint memoir. Cooking together, arguing happily, they sign the first menu. Beat: love and legacy restored.

chapters.title: Epilogue: Signed, Finally
chapters.summary: One year later, at a bookshop reading, Coral introduces the memoir under both their names. A young ghostwriter in the audience asks how she found her voice. Coral smiles: 'I stopped lending it.' Beat: quiet, earned triumph.
